# Nikon

## Brand Overview

Nikon's mirrorless transition centers on the Z-mount system, introduced in 2018. The Z-mount features a notably large 55mm inner diameter (the widest of any full-frame mirrorless mount), which was engineered to maximize optical quality -- particularly sharpness, bokeh, and light-gathering at the edges of the frame. Nikon offers both full-frame (FX) and APS-C (DX) bodies on the Z-mount, sharing the same lens mount.

The Z lens lineup has matured rapidly, covering f/1.2 primes, f/1.8 S-line primes, f/1.4 budget primes, and pro zooms. Third-party support is now expanding: Tamron, Sigma, and Viltrox are producing native Z-mount autofocus lenses, reducing the historical gap versus Sony E-mount. All current Z bodies use the EXPEED 7 processor with deep-learning AF (people/eye/animal detection).

Nikon occupies a strong position for portrait and people photography: excellent skin tones, class-leading eye AF (inherited from the Z9 flagship), and good IBIS across FF bodies.

## Recommended Camera Bodies

Selected for portrait/people photography with emphasis on eye AF, burst capability, and weight.

|-------|--------|-----------|------------|------------|----------------------|---------------|-----|------|----------------|
| Z50 II | APS-C (DX) | 20.9 MP | 520 | $910 | 11 / 30 fps | Yes (EXPEED 7, 209-pt PDAF) | 2.36M-dot OLED, 1000 nits | No | 250 shots |
| Zf | FF (FX) | 24.5 MP | 710 | $1,997 | 14 / 30 fps | Yes (EXPEED 7, subject detect) | 3.69M-dot OLED, 0.8x | Yes (8-stop) | 380 shots |
| Z6 III | FF (FX) | 24.5 MP | 760 | $2,497 | 14 / 20 fps (120 fps DX crop JPEG) | Yes (EXPEED 7, 299-pt PDAF) | 5.76M-dot OLED, 120 Hz, 4000 nits | Yes (8-stop) | 390 shots |
| Z8 | FF (FX) | 45.7 MP | 910 | $3,997 | -- / 20 fps (30 fps JPEG, 120 fps 11MP) | Yes (EXPEED 7, subject detect, -9 EV) | 3.69M-dot OLED, 3000 nits | Yes (6-stop) | 340 shots |

Notes:
- The Z8 has no mechanical shutter (electronic only). Its stacked sensor minimizes rolling shutter.
- The Zf is retro-styled with manual-feel dials; lighter than the Z6 III but has a less advanced EVF and slightly lower burst in electronic raw.
- The Z50 II lacks IBIS but is by far the lightest body. Pair with VR lenses for stabilization.
- The Z6 III uses a partially stacked sensor -- the best EVF in the lineup and the most balanced body for portraits + burst work.

## Lens Recommendations

### Prime Lenses

**35mm equivalent:**
- FF: Nikkor Z 35mm f/1.4 (budget, non-S-line) or Z 35mm f/1.8 S (premium optics)
- APS-C: Nikkor Z DX 24mm f/1.7 (36mm equiv)

**50mm equivalent:**
- FF: Nikkor Z 50mm f/1.2 S (ultimate) or Z 50mm f/1.8 S (best value)
- APS-C: Nikkor Z 35mm f/1.8 S on DX body (~52mm equiv)

**85mm equivalent:**
- FF: Nikkor Z 85mm f/1.2 S (ultimate portrait) or Z 85mm f/1.8 S (compact, excellent)
- APS-C: Nikkor Z 50mm f/1.8 S on DX body (~75mm equiv)

### Zoom Lens (24-70mm equivalent)
- FF: Nikkor Z 24-70mm f/2.8 S or Z 24-70mm f/4 S
- APS-C: Nikkor Z DX 16-50mm f/3.5-6.3 VR (24-75mm equiv)

## System Weight Examples

**Ultralight APS-C portrait kit:**
Z50 II + Z DX 24mm f/1.7 + Z 50mm f/1.8 S = 520 + 135 + 415 = **1,070 g** (two-lens kit covering 36mm and 75mm equiv)

**Balanced FF portrait kit:**
Zf + Z 50mm f/1.8 S + Z 85mm f/1.8 S = 710 + 415 + 470 = **1,595 g** (classic 50/85 combo, IBIS, retro body)

**Pro FF portrait kit:**
Z6 III + Z 24-70mm f/2.8 S + Z 85mm f/1.8 S = 760 + 805 + 470 = **2,035 g** (versatile zoom + portrait prime, best EVF, 8-stop IBIS)

## Key Strengths and Weaknesses

**Strengths:**
- Excellent skin tones and color science; Nikon has long been favored for portrait work
- Large Z-mount diameter enables exceptional prime lens optics (the f/1.8 S primes are class-leading for their size/weight)
- Strong eye/face AF inherited from Z9 flagship across all EXPEED 7 bodies
- The Zf offers a compelling lightweight FF option with retro controls at a competitive price

**Weaknesses:**
- APS-C (DX) native lens lineup is still thin -- only a few DX primes and zooms available; most shooters pair DX bodies with FX lenses (adding weight)
- No IBIS on any DX body (Z50 II, Zfc); stabilization depends on lens VR
- Battery life across the lineup is mediocre (EN-EL15c on FF bodies, smaller EN-EL25a on DX); carry spares
- Third-party Z-mount lens selection, while growing, still trails Sony E-mount and Canon RF in breadth
